task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: shaper role (assumed comparable to the connector role in prior work; not confirmed)
role portability after a team change
methodological_questions: How are 'travel' and portability defined, and is the definition independent of the cut/drive profile label?
Can n=24 units detect the effect sizes seen in earlier work?
Are cut-heavy and drive-heavy labels derived from pre-move data only, and are they compositional mirrors of each other?
How do mover selection, regression to the mean and destination context confound the comparison?
Is 'shaper' the same population as the 'connector' in prior work?

historical_evidence.finding: Among 92 connector movers, pre-move cut share predicted whether the organizational function reproduced after a move (rho=+0.265, p=0.011, AUC 0.653). Cut minus drive gave rho=+0.314, p=0.002. Drive share gave rho=-0.278, p=0.007. The top cut tercile was 65% portable versus 35% in the bottom tercile. Leave-one-out AUC was 0.622 and the permutation p was 0.005. [prior work] lists [prior work] and RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

The connector diet x destination gap-match test had connector subsets of only n=19/40 (n=5/14 matched vs mismatched). The connector delta p was 0.156 and the all-movers binary result (p=0.0283) did not replicate as a continuous Spearman. [prior work] lists the question as not answerable with the design and limited by small sample.

With n=44, the minimum detectable effect at 80% power was about 0.18 PPP (SD~0.34). The observed gap was below the minimum detectable effect, so a true null could not be distinguished from a moderate effect.
Destination net-rating checks for movers were recorded as underpowered and null once corrected for landing-spot quality. No numbers were given, and the check was dropped from Paper 1.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Subgroup tests of connectors (n=19/40) and an all-movers binary test used as a proxy for the connector test
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as small sample and unanswerable. The all-movers significance did not replicate as a continuous association and was not the licensed connector test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: A null-ish comparison at n=44 with outcome measured in PPP
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as low power with a large minimum detectable effect (0.18 PPP), so the null was uninformative.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using destination net rating change as the outcome for movers
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as underpowered, and null after correcting for landing-spot quality.

evidence_establishes: For connector movers (n=92), the earlier family recorded a supported positive association between pre-move cut share and portability, and a negative one for drive share, with a permutation p of 0.005 ([prior work][prior work]).

Earlier project attempts at small-sample mover subgroup tests (n of about 19 to 44) were recorded as untestable or underpowered ([prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]).
evidence_does_not_establish: That the connector result transfers to 'shapers', if shapers are a different or narrower population than connectors.
That the effect is detectable at n=24. [prior work] give no power calculation for this unit count.
That the result is causal or free of destination-context confounding. Only net-rating checks that were corrected for landing-spot quality are recorded, and those were null and underpowered.
Whether [prior work][prior work] had an out-of-sample replication. Only leave-one-out and permutation checks are recorded in the retrieved text.
own_inferences: The question as posed is close to a restatement of the [prior work][prior work] hypothesis, applied to a smaller unit set. This is a replication or extension, not a new question.

Assuming a true rho of about 0.27 to 0.31 (from [prior work][prior work]), power at n=24 is roughly 20-25%. 80% power would need rho of about 0.55. A dichotomous cut-heavy vs drive-heavy comparison with about 12 per group is weaker still.
Cut share and drive share are likely partly mirrored (compositional), so the 'drive-heavy' comparison adds little independent evidence beyond the cut-minus-drive contrast.
The 92 connector movers probably include some or all of the n=24 shapers, so combining them would double-count evidence.
With n=24, a positive point estimate would be fragile to dropping one or two players. [prior work][prior work] itself needed drop-one and top-3 checks.
uncertainties: How 'shaper' is defined, and whether the 24 units are movers, player-seasons or team-seasons.
How 'portable' or 'travel' is operationalised here. The Delta metric in [prior work][prior work] is not described in the retrieved text.
Whether the cut/drive profile and the portability outcome share inputs (the same play-type records).
Whether 2025-26 movers are complete enough to serve as a holdout.
Overlap between the 24 units and earlier samples.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history, the question looks like a fresh test. The retrieved record shows a supported directional result at n=92, which makes a confirmatory, single-contrast replication worthwhile. The other records show small-n tests of similar movers ending untestable. So the decision is proceed_with_changes (one pre-registered contrast, framed as estimation and replication) rather than a free-standing confirmatory test, and a null at n=24 must not be read as rejection.

blocking_constraints.text: n=24 gives roughly 20-25% power for the previously observed rho of about 0.27 to 0.31. A null would be uninformative.
The cut/drive profile and the portability measure both derive from the same play-by-play and play-type records, so shared inputs could produce association without a real portability effect.

prior_work.summary: [prior work][prior work] recorded a supported cut-over-drive portability association for connector movers (n=92). Whether it applies to the 'shaper' subset of 24 is not established. Related small-sample mover tests were recorded as untestable.

risks.text: n=24 gives low power and unstable estimates. Any single player can swing the result.
Cut and drive shares and the portability outcome come from the same derived play-type records. Any shared inputs must be excluded or the outcome measured on independent possessions.
Cut share and drive share are partly compositional mirrors, so 'drive-heavy' is not independent of 'cut-heavy'. Thresholds on them create an arbitrary dichotomy.
The destination team's structural needs, coach, teammates and usage change alongside the move. Earlier net-rating checks were null once landing-spot quality was corrected ([prior work][prior work]).
Movers are a selected group. Shapers with extreme pre-move profiles or outcomes may regress toward the mean, which could mimic or mask a profile effect.
Cut and drive shares and the portability score are noisy at small possession counts. The reliability of the role label is unknown.
Profile features must come from pre-move games only. Post-move or full-season data in the label would leak the outcome.
Many variants are possible (cut share, cut-drive, terciles, position splits, thresholds). Only one primary contrast should be allowed.
Role definitions and league play styles change across 2022-23 to 2025-26. Pooling seasons may mix regimes.

design.estimand: Spearman correlation between the pre-move cut-minus-drive share and the portability change score among shaper movers, with a bootstrap confidence interval. This is treated as a directional replication of [prior work][prior work]. The cut-heavy vs drive-heavy contrast is a secondary descriptive comparison.
design.unit: One shaper mover (a player who changes team between consecutive observed seasons). If one player has several moves, use the earliest or random one, fixed in advance.
design.sample: The n=24 shaper movers in 2022-23 through 2025-26 (regular season plus playoffs where possession counts allow). Pre-specify the shaper definition and the minimum pre- and post-move possession thresholds before looking at outcomes. Report overlap with the 92 connector movers in [prior work][prior work] and do not pool the two. Treat 2025-26 moves as a holdout if the 2025-26 data are complete.
design.power: At n=24 and one-sided alpha=0.05, power for rho=0.27 to 0.31 is about 20-25%, and 80% power would need rho of about 0.55. State this in advance. Report estimates and intervals rather than only p-values. A null or inconclusive result will be labelled inconclusive, not rejected, unless the confidence interval excludes rho of about 0.25.
design.controls: Compute the profile from pre-move possessions only. Compute the portability outcome from post-move possessions and derive it so that it does not share the cut/drive inputs. Adjust for destination structural gap, usage or minutes change, and pre-move possession count, using a partial rank correlation or a small rank-based regression with at most 2-3 covariates given n. Report leave-one-out and drop-top-3 sensitivity.
design.falsification: Permute profile labels 5000 times as in [prior work][prior work]. Run a placebo on a profile feature unrelated to the role (for example pre-move three-point share). Check that the effect does not appear in a pseudo-move pairing of non-movers across consecutive seasons. The hypothesis fails if the point estimate is zero or negative, or if the sign flips under leave-one-out.
design.multiplicity: One primary test (cut-minus-drive rho). The tercile comparison and the drive-only and cut-only shares are secondary and reported without claims. Holm correction applies if more than one is reported as confirmatory. No position splits.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if rho > 0 with the one-sided permutation p < 0.05, the bootstrap lower bound is above 0, and the sign holds in leave-one-out and in the holdout when available. Rejected only if the interval excludes rho of about 0.25 (unlikely at n=24). Otherwise inconclusive, and the best estimate of the effect is reported, not a verdict.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API files and derived play-type possession records for 2022-23 through 2024-25 (regular season and playoffs), 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) and 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21). Freeze the data snapshot and role definitions before analysis, and record the extraction date.
